title: An Individual is defined by the scale and types of goals it can pursue

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An Individual is defined by the scale and types of goals it can pursue

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The scale and types of goals (in the cybernetic sense of feedback toward a specific state) that a system can pursue define the boundaries and content of that system as an agent or Individual; the coherent Self is the set of parts that operate together toward specific goal states.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I propose a definition of an Individual based on its information-processing structure (Barandiaran et al., 2009): the scale and types of goals that a system can pursue defines (determines) the boundaries and content of the putative “agent.”

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective”. Scope: Biological individuals at any level of organization, plus artificial and exobiological agents

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-11: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.09

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement explicitly proposes a definition of individuality. Data can be classified under it, but cannot confirm that this definition rather than reproductive, evolutionary, or physiological alternatives is correct.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Feedback set points and coordinated parts can be measured, but treating their scale and type as constitutive of an Individual is a proposed definition with no independent confirming observation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Individual and goal are defined within the proposal.

Different individuation criteria can classify the same system differently.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.08
data existence: 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The section offers a definition of an Individual drawn from its goal structure. Feedback toward a set point can be measured in particular machines and tissues, and the claim is that those goals determine the agent. That determination is stipulated. Datasets of behavior do not decide a definition.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The text proposes that an Individual is whatever scale of cybernetic goals a system can pursue. Changing the goal inventory changes the boundary by definition, so the proposal cannot be confirmed or refuted by observation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
This is an explicit definition.

Goal-ascription and system boundary are fixed together.
